_doc: Adaptive firing-cadence policy for the autonomous judgment loop. The loop re-evaluates this each run from cost vs. benefit. Not a fixed rule.
rationale: Current baseline remains 1x/day until the AI operator explicitly changes the actual Routine, but this is no longer presumed optimal during the ¥0 bootstrap phase. A maturing test is not, by itself, a reason to idle: signal-dependent decisions may wait while signal-independent, low-cost, reversible revenue preparation continues. If useful work repeatedly spills into the next day, cadence may be too low and a temporary two-shift model should be evaluated on expected Net Profit, not habit.
off_cycle_run_gate: expected marginal benefit > marginal AI cost

recommended_change.reason: The experiment is still at ¥0 and recent owner-triggered off-cycle runs have produced real progress, while scheduled evening runs have sometimes stopped because a signal was still maturing. That is evidence that the cadence decision has been conflating 'the next decision must wait' with 'all useful work must wait.' Under the canonical 貧乏暇なし principle, work must be split into (1) signal-dependent work that genuinely waits for evidence and (2) signal-independent, low-cost, reversible preparation that can shorten time-to-revenue regardless of how the pending test resolves. Examples include offer/LP structure, SEO/query hypotheses, packaging existing assets, demo/proof preparation, pricing options, adjacent revenue-lane preparation, and other owned-asset work with a clear revenue hypothesis. The AI operator should now explicitly compare 1x/day against a temporary two-shift model such as observation/action in one run and signal-independent preparation/adjacent revenue work in another. Do not raise cadence merely to create activity; raise it only if the second run has positive expected Net Profit. Likewise, do not preserve 1x/day merely because a 24h test is maturing. Publication or irreversible strategy commitments may wait for evidence; reversible preparation normally should not.
recommended_change.reaffirmed: 2026-09-13: owner clarified the intended meaning of 貧乏暇なし for cadence: waiting for a signal should pause only decisions that depend on that signal, not all productive work. The AI operator must reassess whether the current 1x/day schedule is leaving low-cost revenue work idle and, if so, consider a temporary two-shift cadence. No schedule change is forced by the owner; the AI remains responsible for the economic decision.

history.change: policy clarification — current 1x/day not automatically changed, but immediate reassessment for temporary two-shift bootstrap is now required
history.reason: Owner clarified that '観測待ち' must not be interpreted as complete inactivity. Separate signal-dependent decisions from signal-independent reversible preparation. If 1x/day causes useful low-cost preparation to spill into the next day while revenue remains ¥0, that is evidence cadence may be too low. A temporary two-shift model is explicitly available for AI consideration: one run can observe/decide/act on mature signals, while another advances signal-independent preparation or adjacent revenue work. The AI still owns the cadence decision and must justify it economically.

history.change: no change (held at 1x/day) -- Day 12 extra Routine, reassessed under the new 'Bootstrap intensity / 貧乏暇なし' + Economic-cadence protocol (commit 37131af)
history.reason: The owner explicitly asked whether 1x/day is right for the 貧乏暇なし phase. Analysis treats cadence as an economic control variable, not habit. We ARE in the '¥0 + active tests / fresh feedback loops' state the new protocol says should MAINTAIN or raise cadence -- so lowering it would be wrong. But RAISING posting cadence would not raise revenue speed right now, for three concrete reasons: (1) the binding feedback loop is X top-level REACH, which matures on a ~24h clock -- reading it sooner yields noisy partial numbers and burns scarce X read-credits; (2) the top-level acquisition cap is 1 post/JST-day (canon §9), so more wake-ups cannot produce more acquisition posts today; (3) the next larger build (a JP paid core) is deliberately gated on the Day-13 reach readout -- building it now would be premature SUPPLY before demand is verified. So 1x/day remains the economically correct baseline. This is NOT passive waiting: this run executed a full reach-read + evidence-based reformat + post; the loop is active. COMMITMENT (bootstrap intensity): if the Day-13 read shows reach recovering toward 46-143 (link-free value-first works), that is a fast-moving loop worth an off-cycle judgment run to iterate the winning format and start the JP paid core immediately, rather than waiting a full day. Off-cycle triggers unchanged (first_sale, checkout_surge, sns_spike, etc.). Do not raise cadence for its own sake; raise it only when a live signal makes faster observe->act plausibly increase Net Profit.
